The two diagonals AC and BD intersect at E inside. In the figure, 28° is labeled at A, 57° is labeled at D along the interior angle of triangle AED, the lower-left corner near intersection point E is labeled as angle 4, and the right side is labeled as angle 5. Angle 5 is the angle between ray EC and ED. Reasoning: In triangle AED, it is known that ∠A = 28°, ∠D = 57°, so ∠AED = 180° - 28° - 57° = 95°. method.method_draft: Label the bottom-left vertex A, top-left vertex B, top-right vertex C, bottom-right vertex D, and the intersection of the two diagonals as E. From the image, read that diagonal AC crosses diagonal BD at E; angle 5 is the angle at E between EC and ED. Also read that in triangle AED, the angle at A is 28° and the angle at D is 57°. Use the triangle angle sum to find angle AED: 180° - 28° - 57° = 95°. Since angle AED and angle 5 share ray ED and their other sides EA and EC are opposite rays on the same straight diagonal AC, they form a linear pair. Therefore angle 5 = 180° - 95° = 85°.
